data.title: Nikkei May Rise After Nvidia Led U.S. Stock Gains — Market Talk
data.description:
1841 ET - Japanese stocks may rise after U.S. stocks surged overnight, led by Nvidia. Nikkei futures are up 3.0% at 57840 on the SGX. The dollar is at 158.98 yen, compared with Y159.17 as of Friday's Tokyo stock market close. Japanese markets were closed Monday for a public holiday. Investors are focusing on crude oil prices and bond yields. The Nikkei Stock Average fell 5.1% to 56436.65 on Friday. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com)

1707 ET - The Mexican peso's recent move above 19 to the U.S. dollar for the first time since June 2025 reflects a narrowing gap between the Bank of Mexico's benchmark interest rate and the U.S. federal funds rate, putting pressure on the peso carry trade, Molly Schwartz and Christian Lawrence of Rabobank say in a note. The Bank of Mexico is expected to hold its benchmark rate at 6.25% next month following November's quarter-point cut, while a quarter-point Fed December increase is widely expected. "We expect the [currency] pair to remain near 19 around the December Fed meeting before easing to 18.8 in three months and around 18.5 by mid-2027, as additional Fed hikes priced by markets fail to materialize," they say. The peso is trading around 19.17 to the dollar. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

1644 ET - The Canadian dollar has weakened to its lowest level relative to USD in about two years, or in the early days of elevated U.S.-Canada trade tensions. USDCAD strengthened to C$1.4369 in Monday trading, according to data provider Tullett Prebon. BMO Capital Markets chief economist Douglas Porter says CAD weakness reflects widening US-Canada short term spreads, of nearly 1.5 percentage points based on respective two-year bond yields. "US growth is much firmer — helped much more by the AI buildout and less hampered by trade unceratinty," Porter says, adding US inflation is also stronger. CAD will remain under pressure until the AI trade "truly ebbs," and more certainty emerges on US-Canada trade front, Porter adds. (paul.vieira@wsj.com, @paulvieira)

1420 ET - Fitch Ratings lowers its U.K. water utilities outlook to deteriorating from improving, citing substantial regulatory uncertainty and other factors. "Uncertainty over the new regulatory framework could affect investor confidence, funding costs and long-term investment, if it persists," Fitch says. The uncertainty includes the regulator's independence, powers and tariff-setting approach, Fitch adds. The agency also points out weak operational and environmental performance may persist in fiscal year 2027. Fitch maintains neutral sector outlooks for the U.K. electricity and gas networks for 2027. (stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com)

1344 ET - Fitch Ratings says public finance ratings would be most affected by a potential one-notch downgrade of France's sovereign rating. Fitch revised France's outlook to negative from stable back in October. The agency says it has now tested the sensitivity of its rated portfolio to a potential one-notch French sovereign downgrade to "A." It found that 90% of French public finance ratings would be downgraded. "A sovereign downgrade would lower the sovereign-capped operating-environment score and would be likely to result in downgrades of BNP Paribas, Crédit Agricole and Crédit Mutuel's regional groups." Implications for structured finance, covered bonds and most supranationals would be limited, according to Fitch.(stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com)

1249 ET - With the holidays coming up, many young adults won't have to travel far to get home, Realtor.com says. A record 25.2 million adults ages 18 to 34 lived with their parents in 2025, or 33% of young adults nationwide, according to Realtor.com. The national share remained just below its 2020 peak of 33.6%. The Northeast had the highest share of young adults living with their parents at 36.9% in 2025, even as the region's rate fell to its lowest level since 2010. While most adults ages 18 to 34 living with their parents are ages 18 to 24, adults ages 25 to 34 have grown as a share of the at-home population since the early 2000s. New York had the highest share of young adults living with their parents among the major metros analyzed, at 41.3%. (chris.wack@wsj.com)

1156 ET - Canadian PM Mark Carney's pledge to double housing construction over a decade faces stiff short-term headwinds, according to an analysis from National Bank of Canada. Economist Daren King says there's a wide gap in Canada between construction costs and housing prices. Until that narrows, housing starts are likely to remain depressed in the near term, He says. Since 4Q of 2019 to 3Q this year, the rise in construction expenses, 73.3%, has outstripped the 30% gain in property prices. The cost for materials account for some of the increase, but the big drivers are unit-labor costs. King's research indicates average-weekly earnings in construction rose over 33% in the 2019-2026 period, versus 29% for all Canadian industries. Meanwhile, construction-sector productivity is 18% lower in Canada relative to prepandemic levels. (paul.vieira@wsj.com; @paulvieira)

1106 ET - Mexico's inflation likely edged up in the first half of November, led by increases in energy as residential electricity subsidies ended in additional cities. El Buen Fin, Mexico's Black Friday-style event that ran Nov. 13-17, could keep a lid on core goods prices. The consumer price index is expected to have risen by 0.50% in the first two weeks of the month, pushing the 12-month inflation rate up to 3.92% from 3.88% in the second half of October, according to a WSJ survey of analysts. Core CPI is expected to have risen 0.10%, moving the annual rate to 3.88% from 3.82% in the second half of October. Statistics institute Inegi is scheduled to report mid-November inflation on Tuesday. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

1105 ET - Home-buying demand dropped last quarter, Zillow says. Mortgage rates rose significantly from July through September, leaving fewer serious shoppers competing for each home on the market. The number of engaged home shoppers per listing, signaling real interest beyond casual browsing, fell to 3.5 nationally in 3Q. That is down 4.8% from a year earlier and the lowest level since the second half of 2023. The pullback was widespread, with engagement down from last year in 44 of the 50 largest metro areas, although major Florida markets were an exception. Mortgage rates are still keeping many buyers on the sidelines, and as inventory continues to build, there is less competition for each home for sale. (chris.wack@wsj.com)

1017 ET - Saudi Arabia's willingness to adjust spending on major development projects is helping contain fiscal risks as the kingdom pursues its Vision 2030 economic diversification program, S&P Global Ratings says. Ravi Bhatia, the agency's lead sovereign analyst, says the government and the Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, have shown flexibility in changing the pace of projects to limit pressure on public finances. Although government debt is rising, Saudi Arabia remains in a net asset position, with financial assets exceeding liabilities, he says in S&P's Middle East Credit Gateway video series. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

1016 ET - Saudi Arabia's banking sector alone won't be able to meet the financing needs of the kingdom's large investment projects, S&P Global Ratings says. Speaking on the agency's Middle East Credit Gateway video series, Hina Shoeb, S&P's head of analytics for Saudi Arabia, says banks are exploring alternative funding sources as demand for financing expands. These include private credit, or loans provided by nonbank investors, structured financing and new Islamic financing arrangements that comply with Sharia principles. The development of alternative funding channels could help support investment beyond what traditional bank deposits can finance. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

1009 ET - Saudi Arabia's ability to redirect oil exports through the Red Sea and its growing nonoil economy are helping protect its creditworthiness despite the Middle East conflict, S&P Global Ratings says. Ravi Bhatia, the ratings agency's lead sovereign analyst, says the kingdom's East-West pipeline, which carries crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, has helped it avoid some disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. Higher oil prices have also supported government revenue. Speaking on S&P's Middle East Credit Gateway video series, Bhatia says the agency expects regional tensions to persist into 2027 but remain largely contained. S&P affirmed Saudi Arabia's A+ rating with a stable outlook in September. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

data.title: CFTC staff say exchanges can count Bitcoin toward operating reserves
data.description:
US Commodity Futures Trading Commission staff said Monday that CFTC-regulated derivative exchanges and clearinghouses can count Bitcoin, Ether and payment stablecoins toward meeting their financial resource requirements.

CFTC rules require derivatives exchanges, swap trading venues and clearinghouses to maintain enough financial resources to cover at least 12 months of operating costs on a rolling basis.

The latest staff guidance clarifies that certain crypto assets can count toward part of that requirement, but with a discount to their market value. CFTC staff said they would accept a “haircut” of at least 20% for Bitcoin and Ether and 2% for qualifying payment stablecoins to account for the risk of holding those assets.

The guidance gives CFTC-regulated exchanges and entities more flexibility in how they meet their operating reserve requirements. CFTC-regulated entities include Coinbase Derivatives, Crypto.com’s North American Derivatives Exchange and Bitnomial Exchange, as well as prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket US.

However, they will still need to meet a separate liquidity requirement with assets such as cash or highly liquid securities.

The advisory represents the views of staff at the Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk, and is not considered a formal rule change approved by the Commission.

data.title: CME live cattle futures firm on surprise in USDA cattle report
data.description:
By P.J. Huffstutter

Live cattle futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange rose on Monday for a fourth consecutive session, after a monthly government report showed a bigger year-on-year drop in the number of cattle in US feedlots than analysts had expected, traders said.

After the market closed Friday, the USDA reported the number of cattle on feed as of November 1 at 99% of a year ago. Analysts surveyed by Reuters on average had expected a smaller decline, to 99.7%.

"It was a pretty wide miss, and the fourth miss in a row in this report from the market's perspective," said Brodrick Schmidt, a commodity broker and market analyst at U.S. Commodities LLC.

The USDA reported cattle placements into US feedlots during October at 93% of a year ago, below the average analyst estimate of 97%. Marketings during October were 95% of a year ago, near the average analyst estimate of 94.9%.

The report told traders that the US is not rebuilding its cattle herd at a brisk pace, Schmidt said, and "that prices will stay strong as long as consumer demand for beef stays strong."

CME December live cattle settled up 1.550 cents at 224.550 cents per pound, and most-active February futures rose 1.050 cents to 228.750 cents.

January feeder cattle fell 1.100 cents to finish at 334.325 cents per pound on technical trading, market analysts said.

Cash cattle markets have seen steady trade and prices firming, with cattle trades reaching $222 per hundredweight, cwt, last week and prices in the north up $7 per cwt, market analysts said.

The wholesale choice boxed beef cutout value rose $3.35 to $356.19 per hundredweight on Monday morning, the USDA said.

Meanwhile, CME lean hog futures closed mostly lower, pressured by sagging cash hog prices and weak demand for pork.

December lean hog futures (LHZ26) settled 0.150 cent lower at 52.450 cents per pound while most-active February hogs (LHG27) dipped to a fresh contract low during the session, before ending up 0.300 cent at 57.275 cents a pound. Four other lean hog contracts also set fresh lows in Monday's trade.

data.title: Austral Resources Hits High-Grade Copper Intersections at Enterprise Deposit
data.description:
Austral Resources Australia has intersected high-grade copper at its Enterprise deposit in Queensland, with initial results supporting further drilling to test extensions beyond the existing resource.

The standout intersection returned 14 metres at 3.00% copper from 118m downhole, including 11m at 3.70%, in the first batch of assays from the 2026 program.

Another hole encountered several zones of copper mineralisation at greater depth, while separate drilling confirmed copper from surface.

The results come from the first six holes of a program intended to improve confidence in the existing deposit and investigate opportunities for resource growth.

High Grades in Multiple Zones

The strongest result contained bornite and chalcocite, which Austral interprets as evidence of localised enrichment along a geological contact that helped channel copper-bearing fluids.

In another hole, drilling intersected 27m at 1.21% copper from 151m, followed by 17m at 1.37% from 197m and 13m at 1.73% from 228m.

Those deeper intersections contain primary copper sulphides rather than the secondary enrichment seen in the standout result, supporting Austral’s interpretation of a higher-grade trend extending downwards.

Near-surface drilling separately returned 28m at 0.61% copper from surface, including 7m at 0.96%, providing additional information for evaluating shallow mineralisation.

The reported intervals are downhole lengths, with true widths estimated at around 60% of those lengths and subject to local variation.

Existing MRE and Untested Strike

Enterprise has an existing inferred mineral resource estimate of 0.95 million tonnes at 0.97% copper using a 0.5% copper cut-off grade.

That estimate reflects historical drilling on sections approximately 120–125m apart across almost 800m of strike, leaving scope for closer-spaced drilling to clarify grade continuity.

Surface copper anomalies extend over approximately two kilometres, considerably beyond the strike covered by the historical resource drilling.

The deposit remains open down dip and down plunge, although the extent and continuity of any additional mineralisation have yet to be established.

Austral is also reviewing historical density assumptions, with further measurements and modelling required before any change to resource tonnage can be assessed.

Resource Growth Drilling

A further 17 percussion holes are planned to examine higher-grade extensions, potential fault-displaced mineralisation northwest of the resource and continuity within the known deposit.

Preliminary metallurgical test work on near-surface oxide and transitional copper mineralisation is being prepared to assess its potential processing characteristics.

New drilling results, geological interpretations, and density measurements are intended to feed into a subsequent update of the Enterprise resource model.

"Enterprise is the latest in a strong run of results from our exploration team this year [that] points to real upside ,not only at Enterprise but across AR's broader tenure, which anchors our organic growth strategy,” chair David Newling said.

“Taken together, Snow Queen, McLeod Hill, Canyon, Waterhole, and now Enterprise show a clear development pathway for the company as it works towards becoming Australia's next mid-tier copper powerhouse."

data.title: CFTC finalises permanent data-reporting rules for event contracts
data.description:
The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission finalized permanent data-reporting rules for certain event contracts on Monday, aiming to strengthen oversight of prediction markets.

  • The rule comes as prediction markets face growing regulatory scrutiny in the US, with questions over federal oversight and market integrity

  • The final rule creates an alternative reporting framework for certain fully collateralised event contracts that have operated under CFTC staff no-action relief since 2017

  • "The CFTC will no longer regulate market participants through a patchwork of no-action letters, which serve as band-aids for unworkable regulations. This final rule is an important step in future-proofing the regulatory framework for event contracts," Chairman Michael Selig said

  • Under the new framework, reporting markets, futures commission merchants, clearing members and foreign brokers will report data under Parts 15-18 of CFTC regulations, instead of relying on reporting provisions spread across Parts 38, 39, 43 and 45

  • The move follows other efforts by the regulator to strengthen federal oversight of prediction markets, including an earlier proposal to classify certain event contracts as swaps

data.title: CAPR Stock Clocks Worst Day Ever After FDA Rejects Approval For DMD Therapy: Company Reportedly Considering ‘Draconian’ Job Cuts
data.description:
Key points:
  • "We're still evaluating that, but it's going to be draconian,” the CEO reportedly said
  • CEO also said that the company is looking to appeal the FDA’s decision to reject approval for the therapy. 
  • The FDA rejected Deramiocel for the second time on Friday, saying Deramiocel’s clinical evidence was insufficient to support approval.

Shares of Capricor Therapeutics (CAPR) slumped 75% on Monday, clocking its worst day ever, after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration rejected its cell therapy for the treatment of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), prompting the company to consider “draconian” job cuts.

The company is now considering potential job cuts that could affect several hundred employees, Reuters reported on Monday, citing CEO Linda Marbán.

"We're still evaluating that, but it's going to be draconian,” the CEO reportedly said, adding that while the FDA has requested a new clinical trial, the company lacks the funding to run it. She also noted that the company is uncertain as to when it can raise the necessary capital, prompting it to consider restructuring. The company currently has 306 full-time employees.

FDA Rejects Capricor’s Deramiocel Again

The FDA rejected Deramiocel for the second time on Friday, saying Deramiocel’s clinical evidence was insufficient to support approval. The agency identified serious data-integrity violations in the company’s late-stage HOPE-3 trial for the therapy, including unauthorized changes to statistical analyses and breaches of procedures designed to prevent bias.

“The correspondence identifies serious data integrity violations in the conduct of Study HOPE-3 that cannot be remediated post-hoc,” it said in a statement. The FDA first rejected approval for the therapy aimed at DMD in July 2025.

DMD is a rare, inherited genetic disorder that causes progressive muscle degeneration and weakness that presents predominantly in young boys. Capricor was seeking approval for the therapy in preserving upper-limb function in patients older than nine this time. Initially, it sought approval for cardiomyopathy associated with DMD.

Capricor Responds

Capricor said on Friday that it disagreed with the FDA, saying it stood behind the integrity of its clinical data and believed the treatment deserved approval. The company also said then that it is reviewing its operating costs to extend cash runway, which is currently expected to fund planned operations for the next 12 months.

"We want to appeal the decision. We think it's wrong," Marbán said in an interview to Reuters on Monday.

How Did CAPR Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around CAPR stock stayed within the 'extremely bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'extremely high' levels.

CAPR stock has slumped 93% year-to-date.

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq End Best Session Since April Last Year On Optimism Led By Jensen Huang’s Reinstatement — NVDA, NASA, TTWO, AMZN In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The S&P 500 gained about 4.7%, the Nasdaq 100 added 6.9%, and the Dow Jones index rose 3% on Monday.
  • Nvidia stock soared 31%, the most since 2003.
  • "I can't wait to get back to work," Huang said.

U.S. stock indices jumped higher on Monday with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq recording their best day since April last year on soaring investor optimism following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO by Nvidia’s board of directors.

The S&P 500 gained about 4.7%, the Nasdaq 100 added 6.9%, and the Dow Jones index rose 3% on Monday. The Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, ended 3.45% higher.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) rose about 4.7%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) added 3.1%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) gained 7% on Monday.

Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF jumped between 13.5% and 16% with Nvidia (NVDA) leading the charts across the board.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘neutral’ on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), ‘extremely bullish’ on the Invesco QQQ (QQQ) and ‘bearish’ on the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA).

US Market Drivers

IndexMoveClose
Dow Jones Industrial Average3%49,595.31
S&P 5004.7%7,237.17
Nasdaq 1006.9%26,746.10

Nvidia’s board, which until last week maintained it would not reinstate Huang to his prior position, reversed its decision and reappointed Jensen Huang as CEO with immediate effect. "I can't wait to get back to work," Huang said.

The dramatic return follows less than a fortnight after Huang stepped down over an admitted relationship with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, which led to a tumultuous stretch during which the semiconductor giant's shares recorded their worst weekly performance since 2008.

Following the announcement, Trump, in a Truth Social post, welcomed the Nvidia board’s decision.

"The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO," Trump wrote, adding that the country needs Huang's leadership to support Nvidia and the broader American economy.

“The reinstatement of the prolific leader of Nvidia’s AI buildout as CEO is bolstering confidence that the momentum of modern technology will remain robust, while sidelining fears of a slowdown,” Jose Torres at Interactive Brokers told Bloomberg.

Key Trending Stocks

Freshly reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will answer questions in an open Senate hearing next week as lawmakers press for answers on American chip export rules and national security safeguards.

U.S. buyers snapped up new video game hardware from Sony and Microsoft at a sharply elevated rate in the week ending Nov. 7, in anticipation of Grand Theft Auto VI, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella said on Monday.

NASA on Monday opened bidding for private industry partners to design, test, and construct the first nuclear fission power plant intended for the lunar surface, targeting a launch-ready system by 2030.

Shares of BridgeBio Pharma (BBIO) rose on Monday after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the company’s oral therapy Welgemda (ribitol) for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 ahead of the deadline.

Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) said Monday it has signed an agreement to purchase the proprietary technology behind AI Startup Decart’s Optimization Stack (DOS) and bring its co-founders and engineering team into the company, as it looks to optimize AI inference and custom silicon performance.

data.title: Court Clears Way for Detonation of Toxic Lead Explosives in Iowa — WSJ
data.description:
By Gareth Vipers and Victoria Albert

A federal appeals court has cleared the way for the U.S. Army to detonate several tons of toxic bomb-making explosives on Wednesday in Iowa.

The Eighth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Monday lifted the temporary hold it had placed on the detonation, finding it was unlikely the environmental groups that sued to stop the explosion would succeed in their challenge.

The Army had previously said it had the authority to move forward despite the hold by using an emergency munitions and explosives exemption under federal environmental law. The ruling nevertheless addresses concerns from President Trump, who earlier Monday said he had told the Army to hold off until it won approval from the court and from Democratic Gov.-elect Rob Sand.

The Army is aiming to conduct a controlled detonation of 9,500 pounds of lead azide, an explosive used in military munitions, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. The detonation, which originally was planned for last week, was rescheduled for the day before Thanksgiving to allow for optimal weather conditions, the Army said.

The Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is in the small city of Middletown, near the state border with Illinois and roughly 160 miles southeast of Des Moines.

In the lawsuit challenging the operation, the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club's Iowa chapter argued the blasts would send a toxic plume of lead dust into the air that could drift up to 100 miles north.

Lead exposure poses severe health risks, particularly to children and pregnant women, including potential damage to the brain and nervous system.

Federal officials have said the blast must occur within the next several days, warning that falling temperatures could destabilize the material and trigger an accidental explosion.

"The Army must perform a controlled detonation to protect the public from the more significant threat from an uncontrolled explosion," the Justice Department said in a court filing Saturday night. The Army had previously delayed plans to destroy the degraded lead azide following pushback from local residents and farmers.

Trump said Monday afternoon that the detonation shouldn't go forward without the court and Sand's approval.

"If he or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation," Trump said on social media.

In a statement on social media, Sand said the administration "should make this decision based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks."

The Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship has advised farmers near the site to move livestock, feed and equipment indoors or relocate them temporarily.

The Army told residents to avoid the area and urged those unable to evacuate to remain indoors, shut windows and doors and turn off heating and cooling systems that draw in outside air.

data.title: Fed's Williams says inflation still too high, signals more rate hikes possible
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fed's Williams points to need for rate hike to cool high inflation
  • Williams says Fed must return inflation to 2% target
  • Williams said policy actions will be tied to data

By Michael S. Derby

New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point the US central bank toward tighter monetary policy, while stressing that the pace of future interest-rate increases will depend on incoming economic data.

"We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis," Williams said in remarks at an event held by the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York. "There is still work to do to get that done."

Williams said inflation is "too high." He noted that he will continue to assess incoming data to decide what action the central bank should take at its December 8-9 policy meeting.

Williams' comments suggested he favors a rate hike at the upcoming meeting. Beyond that, Williams said the path of policy will depend on the economy's performance. “I don't have in my mind a particular timing,” Williams told reporters.

“We're going to have to learn along the way as we get more data,” Williams said, while noting, “I'm not excluding options” when it comes to the cadence of future actions. “I would not exclude, you know, moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed.”

If the economy showed considerable strength and inflation pressures were not moderating, "you wouldn't just want to wait around" and would instead act by adjusting monetary policy, the official said.

DECEMBER HIKE AHOY

Financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point next month from the current 3.75%-4.00% range, with more increases to come next year.

The Fed last raised rates in September as part of an effort to curb inflation, which has been above the 2% target for more than five years. Central bank officials worry that, if this situation persists, the public could lose confidence that inflation will return to that level.

Over recent weeks a wide range of Fed officials have pointed to the need for more rate hikes. Some policymakers have said they'd like to see increases come gradually to allow the economy to adjust, while Fed Governor Christopher Waller has signaled he could support a more aggressive half-percentage-point increase given hot price pressure data.

Williams was speaking the same day as a sharp stock market rally, triggered by chipmaker Nvidia's announcement that it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, after President Donald Trump urged it to do so. Investors' reaction highlighted the importance of AI companies in driving the markets. Some observers had wondered in recent days whether sharp stock losses might deter the Fed from raising rates.

Williams told reporters he was not surprised by the market's volatility and he said that thus far what's happened had not dimmed his optimism about the future of the economy.

Williams also said in his formal remarks that he expects inflation to end the year at 3.5% and to moderate to just above 2% next year before easing to the target in 2028. He also noted that risks to inflation continue to be skewed to the upside and said among the key drivers of high price pressures, energy prices remain elevated and the outlook on that front is uncertain.

He added that "although the effects of tariffs, geopolitical conflicts, and the AI surge are showing up in prices of certain categories of goods, there is little evidence of these spilling over significantly into broader and more persistent inflation."

Williams also said the economy is showing strength and resilience and should grow by 2.75% in both 2026 and 2027. He added that the job market has been showing stability, and the current 4.1% unemployment rate should fall to around 4% next year.

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq End Best Session Since April On Optimism Led By Jensen Huang’s Reinstatement — NVDA, NASA, TTWO, AMZN In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The S&P 500 gained about 4.7%, the Nasdaq 100 added 6.9%, and the Dow Jones index rose 3% on Monday.
  • Nvidia stock soared 31%, the most since 2003.
  • "I can't wait to get back to work," Huang said.

U.S. stock indices jumped higher on Monday with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq recording their best day since April last year on soaring investor optimism following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO by Nvidia’s board of directors.

The S&P 500 gained about 4.7%, the Nasdaq 100 added 6.9%, and the Dow Jones index rose 3% on Monday. The Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, ended 3.45% higher.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) rose about 4.7%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) added 3.1%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) gained 7% on Monday.

Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF jumped between 13.5% and 16% with Nvidia (NVDA) leading the charts across the board.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘neutral’ on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), ‘extremely bullish’ on the Invesco QQQ (QQQ) and ‘bearish’ on the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA).

US Market Drivers

IndexMoveClose
Dow Jones Industrial Average3%49,595.31
S&P 5004.7%7,237.17
Nasdaq 1006.9%26,746.10

Nvidia’s board, which until last week maintained it would not reinstate Huang to his prior position, reversed its decision and reappointed Jensen Huang as CEO with immediate effect. "I can't wait to get back to work," Huang said.

The dramatic return follows less than a fortnight after Huang stepped down over an admitted relationship with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, which led to a tumultuous stretch during which the semiconductor giant's shares recorded their worst weekly performance since 2008.

Following the announcement, Trump, in a Truth Social post, welcomed the Nvidia board’s decision.

"The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO," Trump wrote, adding that the country needs Huang's leadership to support Nvidia and the broader American economy.

“The reinstatement of the prolific leader of Nvidia’s AI buildout as CEO is bolstering confidence that the momentum of modern technology will remain robust, while sidelining fears of a slowdown,” Jose Torres at Interactive Brokers told Bloomberg.

Key Trending Stocks

Freshly reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will answer questions in an open Senate hearing next week as lawmakers press for answers on American chip export rules and national security safeguards.

U.S. buyers snapped up new video game hardware from Sony and Microsoft at a sharply elevated rate in the week ending Nov. 7, in anticipation of Grand Theft Auto VI, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella said on Monday.

NASA on Monday opened bidding for private industry partners to design, test, and construct the first nuclear fission power plant intended for the lunar surface, targeting a launch-ready system by 2030.

Shares of BridgeBio Pharma (BBIO) rose on Monday after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the company’s oral therapy Welgemda (ribitol) for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 ahead of the deadline.

Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) said Monday it has signed an agreement to purchase the proprietary technology behind AI Startup Decart’s Optimization Stack (DOS) and bring its co-founders and engineering team into the company, as it looks to optimize AI inference and custom silicon performance.

data.title: Strathcona Resources and Greenfire Resources Announce Filing of Joint Management Information Circular and Receipt of Interim Order
data.description:
Calgary, Alberta--(Newsfile Corp. - November 23, 2026) - Strathcona Resources Ltd.  ("Strathcona") and Greenfire Resources Ltd.   ("Greenfire") are pleased to jointly announce that Strathcona and Greenfire obtained an interim order of the Court of King's Bench earlier today, November 23, 2026, and have each filed the joint management information circular (the "Joint Circular") dated November 23, 2026 and related meeting and proxy materials in connection with the proposed arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (the "Arrangement"). The Arrangement provides for, among other matters, the acquisition by Strathcona of all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Greenfire pursuant to the arrangement agreement between Strathcona and Greenfire dated effective November 8, 2026.

The meeting materials will be mailed shortly to holders of common shares of each of Strathcona ("Strathcona Shareholders") and Greenfire ("Greenfire Shareholders", and together with Strathcona Shareholders, "Shareholders") of record as of November 23, 2026. The Joint Circular, as well as the Schedule 13E-3 transaction statement (which includes the Joint Circular and related proxy materials), is available under each of Strathcona and Greenfire's SEDAR+ profiles at www.sedarplus.ca and on Greenfire's EDGAR profile at www.sec.gov, as well as on their respective websites, at https://www.strathconaresources.com and https://www.greenfireres.com.

Special Meeting Details

Strathcona will hold a special meeting (the "Strathcona Meeting") to approve the Arrangement on January 12, 2027 at 10:00 a.m. (Calgary time) at the offices of Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP, Suite 3500, 855 - 2nd Street S.W., Calgary, Alberta, T2P 4J8. Greenfire will hold a special meeting (the "Greenfire Meeting" and, together with the Strathcona Meeting, the "Meetings") to approve the Arrangement on January 12, 2027 at 9:00 a.m. (Calgary time) at the offices of Bennett Jones LLP, Suite 4500, 855 - 2nd Street S.W., Calgary, Alberta, T2P 4K7.

The boards of directors of Strathcona and Greenfire have each unanimously recommended their minority Shareholders vote for the applicable Arrangement resolution.

Shareholders are encouraged to vote well in advance of the Meetings, whether or not a Shareholder is intending to attend the Meetings in person. Details on how to vote can be found in the Joint Circular under the sections "General Information Concerning The Strathcona Meeting And Voting" and "General Information Concerning The Greenfire Meeting And Voting". Voting will open immediately following the mailing of the meeting materials, expected to be on or about December 1, 2026.

Strathcona and Greenfire have each retained Laurel Hill Advisory Group ("Laurel Hill") as its proxy solicitation agent in connection with the Meetings. Shareholders with questions or who require assistance voting are encouraged to contact Laurel Hill by calling 1 877 452 7184 (toll free in North America) or +1 416 304 0211 (outside North America), texting "INFO" to either number, or by emailing assistance@laurelhill.com.

About Strathcona

Strathcona is one of North America's fastest growing pure play heavy oil producers with operations focused on thermal oil and enhanced oil recovery. Strathcona is built on an innovative approach to growth achieved through the consolidation and development of long-life assets. Strathcona's common shares (symbol SCR) are listed on the TSX.

For more information about Strathcona, visit www.strathconaresources.com.

Investor inquiries:

info@strathconaresources.com.

Media inquiries:

communications@strathconaresources.com.

About Greenfire

Greenfire is an oil sands producer actively developing its long-life and low-decline thermal oil assets in the Athabasca region of Alberta, Canada, with its registered office in Calgary, Alberta. Greenfire plans to leverage its large resource base and significant infrastructure in place to drive meaningful, capital-efficient production growth. Greenfire common shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the Toronto Stock Exchange under the trading symbol "GFR".

For more information, visit www.greenfireres.com.

investors@greenfireres.com.
